title: Good manners around the world
examples: What is a polite way to say hello in different countries?
Do people have different rules for eating food?
Should I bring a gift when I visit someone new?

explain.say: Today we learn about good manners around the world. Manners change when you travel to new places.
First we look at greetings. Some cultures prefer a handshake for saying hello. This is common in many Western countries.
Next we learn about eating manners. In some places, it is polite to eat with your right hand. Always check what is expected.
Our third topic is giving gifts. When you give a gift, it is often important to use both hands to present it. This shows respect.
In everyday life, if you visit a friend in Japan, you might bow your head to greet them. Bowing is a common and respectful way to say hello there.
A common mistake is assuming all cultures greet the same way. Always remember to observe and ask politely first.

items: Ask a trusted person for advice.

draw.text: Mistake: Assuming all manners are same.

faq.q: Do I always have to bow when I travel?
faq.a: No, you do not always have to bow everywhere you go. It is best to watch what the people around you are doing first.

faq.q: Is it okay to use my left hand sometimes?
faq.a: In many cultures, using the left hand for eating or passing things is considered impolite. It is safest to use your right hand.
asks: Can I use my left hand?

faq.q: What kind of gift is always safe to give?
faq.a: When in doubt, small, useful items are often appreciated. The thought behind the gift is usually more important than the gift itself.
asks: Do I need to buy a gift?

faq.q: Are there different rules for greetings in Asia?
faq.a: Yes, greetings can vary greatly across Asia. Some cultures use bows, while others use specific hand gestures.
asks: How do people greet in Asia?

faq.q: What if I forget the local custom?
faq.a: If you forget a custom, a simple smile and an apologetic gesture usually work well. People appreciate the effort you are making.
asks: How do I apologize for manners?

facts: In some cultures, direct eye contact can be seen as rude.
When giving gifts, presenting them with both hands shows respect.
Eating with the right hand is a custom in many parts of Asia.
Bowing is a common greeting in Japan and Korea.

quiz.say: If you are in a culture where bowing is common, what is the best greeting to use?
quiz.show: Bowing is respectful in some places.
quiz.why: Bowing is a specific, recognized gesture of respect in many Asian cultures.

wrong.0: Shaking hands is common in Western cultures but might not be appropriate everywhere.
wrong.1: Waving is informal and might not show enough respect in formal settings.
wrong.2: A smile is good, but it does not replace a specific cultural greeting gesture.

quiz.say: When passing food to someone, which hand is generally considered polite in many cultures?
quiz.show: Use the right hand for passing items.
quiz.why: The right hand is traditionally used for eating and giving things to show cleanliness and respect.

wrong.1: The left hand is often associated with less clean tasks in many cultures.
wrong.2: Using both hands is good for presenting gifts, but the right hand is usually sufficient for simple passing.
wrong.3: Manners require paying attention to local customs rather than just convenience.

quiz.say: When presenting a gift, what is the most polite action?
quiz.why: Using both hands when giving a gift shows extra care and deep respect for the recipient.

wrong.1: Simply handing it over can appear too casual or thoughtless.
wrong.2: One hand can sometimes imply less importance or respect for the person.
wrong.3: Placing it down first makes the act of giving less personal.
